high_consensus.description: This is a real and high-risk gap: schema/migration ordering can break validation during rollout if not explicitly staged. The proposed fix is concrete (separate migration step, gating/flag, or version bump) and cheap relative to outage risk.

Valuable for auditability and reproducible cost analysis, especially since several requirements depend on numeric comparisons. Trade-off: hardcoded pricing in PRDs can stale quickly, so a 'frozen snapshot reference' is better than embedding many mutable numbers inline.

Strong operational improvement. Kill-switch precedence ambiguity is a classic incident-time failure mode; explicitly defining env-vs-config precedence and layer order is low effort and high reliability payoff.

Practical reliability gap: endpoint changes often alter rate-limit and timeout behavior. Reusing old retry policy without explicit validation is risky. Moderate implementation cost, meaningful production impact.

High-value clarification with very low cost. If streaming is out of scope, the request contract must explicitly disable it; otherwise behavior can fail in subtle ways. This is precise and easy to enforce in tests.

blockers.concern: Alias-level kill-switch may not protect users who call concrete model IDs directly
blockers.why_matters: Rollback assumes alias resolution control, but some downstream consumers may bypass aliases. Incident recovery could be partial, leaving mixed behavior during outages.
blockers.location: Executive Summary kill-switch design and FR-1 acceptance criteria
blockers.recommendation: Document and test rollback behavior for direct model-id users; add an optional provider/model deny policy switch for emergency hard blocks.

blockers.concern: Cost-safe default claim is undermined by gpt-5.5 still using /v1/responses with potential reasoning_tokens billing
blockers.why_matters: PRD asserts gpt-5.5 (non-pro) is cost-safe but doesn't confirm whether non-pro gpt-5.5 returns reasoning_tokens or not. If it does (even at lower volume), the 'cost-safe default' claim is false and downstream consumers who pin-bump will see unexpected cost increases. Probe evidence cited only confirms gpt-5.5-pro returns reasoning_tokens.
blockers.location: FR-2, §3.1 Response Contract Matrix, Executive Summary
blockers.recommendation: Before Sprint 2 merge, run a controlled cost-comparison probe (same prompt, gpt-5.3-codex vs gpt-5.5 vs gpt-5.5-pro) and document actual delta. If gpt-5.5 returns reasoning_tokens at any volume, update CHANGELOG with concrete numbers, not '~Δ%' placeholder.

blockers.concern: Eight caller files updated by hand creates drift risk; SSOT-derived generation incomplete
blockers.why_matters: PRD says 'eight files hardcode gpt-5.3-codex' and they will be 'updated to reference new defaults via SSOT-derived generated-model-maps.sh'. But hardcoded yq fallback strings, agent bindings, and doc samples are NOT auto-generated — they're manually edited. One missed file = silent inconsistency where some code paths use new alias, others use old.
blockers.location: FR-2 acceptance criteria, Problem Statement 'Current State'
blockers.recommendation: Add a CI check / pre-merge bats test that greps for literal 'gpt-5.3-codex' across the repo and fails if found outside allowlisted locations (registry self-map entry, backward-compat tests, CHANGELOG history). Make the allowlist explicit in the test.

blockers.concern: Fail-fast reliability requirement conflicts with automatic Gemini fallback demotion behavior
blockers.why_matters: NFR says UNAVAILABLE should fail-fast with no silent fallback, but FR-4 introduces automatic fallback. This contradiction can produce unpredictable runtime behavior and debugging confusion.
blockers.location: Non-Functional Requirements: Reliability vs FR-4 acceptance criteria
blockers.recommendation: Define a single policy matrix per provider/model class (fail-fast vs fallback) and enforce it explicitly in config schema and tests.

blockers.concern: Guardrail ordering is ambiguous: Sprint 2 introduces cost primitives but Sprint 2 also flips high-traffic aliases
blockers.why_matters: Any sequencing mistake inside Sprint 2 can expose users to unexpected cost spikes before caps/denylist are active, especially in multi-PR merges.
blockers.recommendation: Split Sprint 2 into enforceable sub-milestones with CI gates: (1) guardrails merged and released first, (2) alias flips enabled only after guardrail verification in a tagged build.

blockers.concern: Response parsing is brittle to unrecognized /v1/responses shapes and currently fails hard on unknown output types
blockers.why_matters: The PRD explicitly limits support to six observed shapes and raises UnsupportedResponseShapeError for anything else. If OpenAI adds or changes a shape, core reviewer/reasoning flows can break immediately in production.
blockers.location: Technical Considerations §3.1 and Scope: 'Future OpenAI response object types... out of scope'
blockers.recommendation: Add a forward-compatible parser path (capture raw block + degrade gracefully), contract-version monitoring, and canary tests against live /v1/responses to detect drift before broad rollout.

blockers.concern: Rolling-model policy introduces nondeterministic quality/cost changes after release
blockers.why_matters: Using rolling aliases for runtime means behavior can change without repo changes, reducing reproducibility and making regressions hard to root-cause.
blockers.location: Constraints: Snapshot pinning policy and Compliance: Stay rolling
blockers.recommendation: Add optional runtime snapshot pin mode for production/CI and automated drift alerts when upstream model metadata or behavior changes.

blockers.concern: Session cost-cap semantics are underdefined (what is a session across concurrent agents/processes?)
blockers.why_matters: Without strict scoping, max_cost_per_session_micro_usd may under-enforce or over-enforce. In distributed CI or parallel workflows, budgets can be bypassed or trigger false stops.
blockers.location: FR-5a and FR-5 optional cost cap requirements
blockers.recommendation: Specify session identity, lifecycle, concurrency semantics, and persistence boundaries; add integration tests for parallel calls and process restarts.
